mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 4 Series 420i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full BMW 420i engine replacement typically costs between £1,800 and £5,800 for the engine itself, depending on whether you choose used, reconditioned or rebuilt. Specialist fitting adds £650-£910 in labour. Used N20B20U0: £1,200-£2,200. Reconditioned B48B20A: £2,800-£4,500. Rebuilt B48B20A: £3,800-£5,800.

mainEntity.name: Does the BMW 4 Series 420i have timing chain problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early N20-powered 420i models (2013-2016) are known for timing chain guide failure, typically between 60,000-90,000 miles. The B48 engine introduced in 2016 addressed this design flaw and is significantly more reliable. Rattling noise on cold start is the primary warning sign. Preventative chain replacement costs £1,200-£1,800 at a specialist.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 4 Series 420i?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 420i worth over £8,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine (£2,800-£5,800) is a sound investment that can extend the car's life by 100,000+ miles. For cars under £5,000, a used engine (£1,200-£2,200) with a preventative timing chain replacement before fitting is often the most cost-effective route. Always factor in fitting costs (£650-£910).

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my BMW 420i has the N20 or B48 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The engine change happened during 2016, with LCI models featuring the B48. The easiest way to check is by decoding your VIN - the last seven digits will reveal the engine code. Alternatively, the B48 has a noticeably different engine cover design. Pre-2016 models typically have the N20B20U0. 2016-onwards LCI models have the B48B20A.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 4 Series 420i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 420i engine replacement takes 10-14 hours of workshop labour. With parts sourcing and scheduling, allow 2-5 working days from order to completion. Supply-only: 1-3 working days for delivery. Supply & fit: 3-5 working days total.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 420i and 430i engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 420i uses a 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo producing 184hp, while the 430i uses a higher-output version of the same B48 engine producing 258hp. Both are from the same engine family, but the 430i has different turbocharger calibration and internals. The 420i is more fuel-efficient with lower purchase cost; the 430i is significantly faster (0-62mph in 5.6s vs 7.3s).

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 4 Series 420i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 420i launched as the entry-level petrol variant of the first-generation 4 Series (F32/F33/F36) in November 2013, powered initially by the N20 four-cylinder turbo. In 2016, BMW replaced the N20 with the more robust B48 engine as part of the Life Cycle Impulse (LCI) update, bringing improved reliability and emissions compliance. The second-generation G22 420i (2020-present) continues with an updated B48 variant.

milestones.description: N20B20U0, 2.0L turbocharged inline-four, 184hp, launch of F32 420i Coupe
F33 420i Convertible and F36 420i Gran Coupe join the range
B48B20A replaces N20B20U0 across all 420i body styles; LCI update brings improved timing chain design and Euro 6 compliance
G22 420i launched with B48B20B / B48B20M1, 184hp, mild-hybrid technology on later models
present - G22 LCI 420i continues with refined B48 powertrain

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 4 Series 420i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 4 Series 420i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 420i's engine reliability varies significantly by generation. Early N20-powered cars (2013-2016) are known for timing chain issues, while the B48 engine (2016 onwards) is considerably more robust. For 420i owners facing major engine failure, rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why the BMW 4 Series 420i N20 Engine Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Plastic timing chain guides become brittle with heat cycling and oil degradation, causing them to break. The chain then stretches or snaps, leading to valve/piston interference and catastrophic engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, guides, tensioner and oil pump drive module
repairOptions.longevity: Best value if caught early - prevents engine destruction

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has already snapped or engine is damaged

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Apply this UK-wide decision framework to your BMW 4 Series 420i: - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: a used engine or preventative chain replacement typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise on cold start from your N20-powered 420i, act immediately - a £1,200-£1,800 preventative chain replacement is far cheaper than a £3,200+ engine replacement. For B48-powered cars (2016 onwards), the risk is significantly lower, but regular oil changes using the correct BMW Longlife spec are essential.

problems.group: Oil Consumption & Valve Stem Seal Wear
problems.h4: Oil Consumption & Valve Stem Seal Wear - BMW 420i B48 and N20
problems.rootCause: On N20 engines, valve stem seals can harden and allow oil past the valves. On B48 engines, excessive consumption may indicate worn piston rings or PCV system issues.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace PCV valve (integrated into valve cover on some variants)
repairOptions.longevity: First step for B48 oil consumption

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve stem seals without removing cylinder head (specialist tool)
repairOptions.longevity: N20 engines with blue smoke on startup

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete strip-down, new piston rings, bearings, seals
repairOptions.longevity: Severe cases where oil consumption exceeds 1L/1,000 miles

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a BMW 420i worth £6,000-£12,000, valve stem seal replacement at a specialist (£1,200-£2,000) is a sensible investment. Full rebuild only makes sense for cars worth over £8,000 or with strong sentimental/commercial value.
problems.recommendation: Monitor oil levels regularly - the B48 typically consumes 0.5-1 litre per 10,000 miles, which is within normal parameters. If consumption exceeds this, start with a PCV system inspection (£200-£400) before committing to more expensive work.
